newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvia finmin backs more balanced budgets.
newsitem.headline: New Latvia finmin backs more balanced budgets.

text.p: New Latvian Finance Minister Robert Zile, earlier voted into office by parliament, said on Thursday that he would like to see more balanced budgets to add to the one passed for 1997.

Zile gained the backing of 64 of parliament's 100 MPs and four voted against his appointment. He is from the third-largest party of the eight-party government and is currently head of the budget and finance committee.
"I would like to see a normal balanced budget also for next year and some conceptual matters to be clarified already for 1999," Zile told Latvian radio after the vote.
He said that he would also see a tax system that was more predictable and which changed only with changes in the budget or in the new calandar year.
Zile also said he backed a transparent system, so that people could see clearly where money was being spent.
"Any spare funds that the budget receives should be spent on social services and on the improvement of the state revenue service. This is what earns money," he added.
The finance post has been vacant since October and a row over a previous appointment caused the fall of the former government of Prime Minister Andris Shkele.
